key_insight: A domain-specific language of symbolic predicates helps LLM agents reason more reliably during inverse materials design by grounding natural-language rules in statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: This approach could speed up discovery of high-performance perovskite oxides by enabling interpretable, data-grounded design without task-specific training.
method: Translate natural-language design rules into chemistry DSL predicates.
Use accumulated materials data to test, validate, or reject rules during the design loop.
Run a multi-agent framework (ORCHESTRA) for iterative inverse design of double perovskite oxides.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that DSL-guided agents improved rule validation and showed better performance than natural-language-only prompting, especially for harder target properties.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the stored materials data, so weak data support may still limit rule grounding and design reliability.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
